whatItIs.text: An evergreen Mediterranean shrub with pine-needle leaves — botanically reclassified into the Salvias in 2017, but the kitchen never noticed.

historyNote.text: Its Latin name ros marinus means 'sea-dew', and rosemary thrives by the sea; the Romans probably brought it to Britain in 43 CE, Charlemagne ordered it grown in monastic gardens, and the first British naturalisation record is 1338, when cuttings were sent to Queen Philippa by her mother.

howToChoose.text: Choose stiff, deeply green sprigs that release resinous scent when bent; grey-brown or brittle needles are spent.

storage.text: Wrap in damp paper in the fridge crisper, or dry the sprigs.

useItUp.text: Woody sprigs are for infusing: lay over roasts, steep in oil or honey, or tuck under chicken skin; strip dried leaves and grind for rubs.
